_comment: Shared decode test vectors for the Rust step_encoding and TS ifc-string decoders. Expected values use JSON unicode escapes so this file stays pure ASCII. Both decoders must agree on every case.

cases.name: backslash_pair_is_one_backslash
cases._comment: #2323. ISO 10303-21 doubles the reverse solidus inside a string literal, so a doubled backslash is ONE backslash. Neither decoder collapsed it before.

cases.name: backslash_pair_doubled
cases._comment: Two escaped backslashes are two literal backslashes - exactly one collapsing pass, never a repeated one.

cases.name: directive_then_escaped_backslash
cases._comment: A directive followed by an escaped backslash ends in THREE backslashes. The directive must consume its own \X0\ terminator first; a pre-pass collapsing pairs left-to-right would eat it and leave an unterminated \X2\.

cases.name: escaped_backslash_then_literal_directive_text
cases._comment: The mirror case: an escaped backslash followed by the literal characters X2\00FC\X0\ is NOT a directive, so that text survives verbatim.

cases.name: malformed_x4_empty_payload
cases._comment: An empty hex payload is not a directive, so what remains is a doubled reverse solidus plus a dangling terminator backslash.

cases.name: doubled_quote_is_NOT_touched_by_the_decoder
cases._comment: Contract pin: '' is un-doubled by the tokenizer's consumers BEFORE they call the decoder (see literal_cases). If a decoder collapsed it here too, those callers would double-collapse.

cases.name: s_escape_non_bmp_parity
cases._comment: Malformed: \S\ is spec-defined for ASCII only. Pins that both decoders read the whole code point (U+1F600) plus 128 (=U+1F680) and advance past the surrogate pair, rather than diverging on a trailing surrogate.

_literal_comment: END-TO-END cases (#2323). `raw` is a STEP string literal's INNER bytes, exactly as the tokenizer hands them over with '' still doubled; `value` is what a consumer must surface. The two decoders agreeing is not enough: the '' escape is delegated to the caller, so the contract only holds if callers un-double FIRST and then decode. Rust drives these through AttributeValue::from_token, TS through decodeIfcString(raw.replace(/''/g, "'")).

literal_cases.name: four_quotes_are_two_apostrophes
literal_cases._comment: Over-collapse guard: exactly ONE un-doubling pass. A second would turn this into a single apostrophe.

literal_cases.name: order_proof_two_separately_escaped_apostrophes
literal_cases._comment: ORDER PROOF. Un-double THEN decode yields two apostrophes (correct: two independent \X\27 escapes). Decode THEN un-double yields ONE, silently losing a character.

literal_cases.name: order_proof_s_escape_over_a_doubled_quote
literal_cases._comment: ORDER PROOF. Un-double THEN decode makes the \S\ operand an apostrophe (0x27+128 = U+00A7). Decode THEN un-double consumes only the first quote as the operand and leaves a stray second one.
